title: Multi-TAP: Multi-criteria Target Adaptive Persona Modeling for Cross-domain Recommendation

problem.claim: Cross-domain recommendation aims to alleviate data sparsity by transferring knowledge across domains.

gap.claim: Existing methods primarily rely on coarse-grained behavioral signals and often overlook intra-domain heterogeneity in user preferences.

contributions.claim: Multi-TAP is a multi-criteria target-adaptive persona framework that captures intra-domain preference heterogeneity through semantic persona modeling.
Multi-TAP selectively incorporates source-domain signals conditioned on the target domain to preserve relevance during knowledge transfer.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world datasets reportedly show that Multi-TAP consistently outperforms state-of-the-art cross-domain recommendation methods.
The authors report that the Multi-TAP codebase is available on GitHub.

narrative_sequence.summary: Cross-domain recommendation addresses data sparsity through cross-domain knowledge transfer, but existing methods miss fine-grained preference heterogeneity.
Multi-TAP models heterogeneous preferences with semantic personas and adapts source-domain signal selection to the target domain.
Experiments on real-world datasets are reported to show consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods.
The codebase is reported as publicly available.

source_observation.claim: Source-domain signals are selected conditionally on the target domain.

interpretation.claim: Transfer mechanisms may benefit from adapting signal selection to the receiving domain rather than transferring all source information uniformly.

application.claim: For cross-domain transfer systems, condition source-signal selection on target-domain relevance when source information may be heterogeneous.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether target-adaptive selection helps when domains are already closely aligned or when source signals are uniformly relevant.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, evaluation metrics, baseline methods, or numerical gains.
The abstract does not describe the multi-criteria persona construction or signal-selection mechanism in detail.
The abstract does not provide ablations, computational costs, or limitations.
